subtype: Approach: stops, records the lessons and redirects the effort [Revision]
passage:
Sunday night. Today I closed the app. Turned off the servers, sent the last email to users, and hugged Ankita at the doorway. It hurt more than I expected. Then, before the feeling could settle, I opened a notebook and wrote two pages headed What I learned. About the market: people wanted a cheap, simple tool, not our long list of features. About us: we never spoke openly when the numbers dropped, and we hired before we knew the need. I underlined three lessons. Ankita is going to help with the next idea: a small tool, one feature, and a check with real users in the first month. It is smaller. It feels lighter.

Uday

qa.a: Uday wrote two pages headed What I learned, about the market and about the team.

qa.q: How did Uday feel about closing the app?
qa.a: Uday felt hurt, more than expected, and also a sense of lightness about the smaller plan.

qa.q: How could Uday use the lessons?
qa.a: Uday could use them to build a one-feature version with an early user check, and talk openly with Ankita when numbers drop.

qa.q: How might Ankita feel on the day the app closed?
qa.a: Ankita may feel sad about the closing but hopeful, and glad to help with the next idea.

grounding: Shows a founder closing a product, writing down what was learned about the market and the team, and redirecting effort to a smaller venture.
